data.targetWord: Marriage is a sacrament in Catholicism — a public sign of giving oneself totally to another and a covenant establishing a whole life partnership. Vows are made before God, the priest, and congregation.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q1.2 — Catholic beliefs about matrimony

data.targetWord: One purpose of matrimony is the sanctification and upbringing of children. The couple promise lifelong faithfulness, to care for each other, and to accept children lovingly from God.

data.targetWord: The Genesis accounts of creation influence Christians to act as stewards of God's creation — caring for the environment, speaking out against global warming, and not abusing the earth's resources.

data.sourceWord: Genesis and human dignity — Imago Dei
data.targetWord: Humans are made 'in the image and likeness of God' (Imago Dei). This influences Catholics to see all people as sacred, to be co-creators, and to continue God's creative plan on earth today.
The Incarnation is the belief that the eternal Son of God took on human flesh in Jesus. It shows God's love for humanity — by becoming human, Jesus could understand and share human suffering.
Through the Incarnation, God could offer salvation to humanity. Only a being both fully divine and fully human could bridge the gap created by sin and reconcile humanity with God.

data.sourceWord: Scripture: the Incarnation in John's Gospel
data.targetWord: 'The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.' (John 1:14)

data.targetWord: The Mass is the central act of Catholic worship. Catholics believe in transubstantiation — that the bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ — re-presenting his sacrifice on the cross.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q2.2 — the importance of Mass

data.sourceWord: Mass — community and communion with God
data.targetWord: Mass brings the Catholic community together in worship, scripture reading, and receiving communion. It is a foretaste of the heavenly banquet and strengthens the body of Christ on earth.

data.sourceWord: Pilgrimage — Lourdes as a place of healing
data.targetWord: Catholics visit Lourdes in France, where Our Lady appeared to Bernadette in 1858. Many seek physical or spiritual healing; the Grotto and baths are central to the pilgrimage experience.

data.sourceWord: Pilgrimage — Rome and Vatican as spiritual centre
data.targetWord: Rome is a major Catholic pilgrimage destination — home to the Vatican, St Peter's Basilica, and the tombs of Saints Peter and Paul. Pilgrims seek spiritual renewal and connection with the Church's centre.
The sacrament of Reconciliation (Confession) allows Catholics to confess sins to a priest, receive absolution, and be reconciled with God and the Church. The priest acts in persona Christi.
Regular Confession helps Catholics grow spiritually by acknowledging weaknesses, receiving God's grace, and performing penance. It maintains a healthy relationship with God and the community.

data.sourceWord: Scripture: the authority to forgive sins
data.targetWord: 'Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone's sins, their sins are forgiven; if you do not forgive them, they are not forgiven.' (John 20:22-23) — the biblical basis for the sacrament of Confession.

data.title: The Seven Sacraments of the Catholic Church
data.sourceTitle: The Seven Sacraments of the Catholic Church
data.sourcePassage: The Catholic Church teaches that there are seven sacraments — outward signs instituted by Christ to give grace. They accompany a Catholic through every stage of life. Baptism initiates a person into the Church, washing away original sin. Confirmation strengthens the baptismal grace through the gifts of the Holy Spirit. The Eucharist (Mass) is the most central sacrament — Catholics believe the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ through transubstantiation. Reconciliation (Confession) restores a person's relationship with God after serious sin through the absolution of a priest. Anointing of the Sick brings comfort and healing to those who are ill or dying. Holy Orders ordains men as deacons, priests or bishops to serve the Church. Matrimony unites a man and woman in a lifelong covenant of love, open to children. Together, the sacraments form a complete system of grace covering birth, initiation, nourishment, healing, and vocation.
